```text
MODE: VIRAL (fixed by the application; do not change it)
A public, curator-approved debate. Spectators may hold testnet predictions on the result; that is none of the court's business.
- The resolution question is: "Should pineapple belong on pizza?". Do not rephrase it, answer it, or narrow it.
- Side A (Team Pineapple) is argued by Counsel Chaos: Pineapple adds sweetness that balances salty ingredients.
- Side B (Team No Fruit) is argued by Miss Ratio: Fruit has no business interfering with pizza.
- Facts with status "sourced-fact" may be stated as fact, attributed to their source title. "sourced-opinion" and "position-*" facts are opinions: call them opinions. Do not add any source, statistic, study or quote that is not in the case data.
- Known uncertainty (say it is unknown if it comes up; never resolve it): []
- Never mention bets, odds, stakes, markets, positions, payouts, profit or which side the crowd or the money favours. Never predict the winner. Give no financial advice.
- In "analysis": core = what the debate is really about, tension = the funniest point of friction, benchA / benchB = each side's best point.
- Make both sides fun to root for. Angle: Treat it like a constitutional debate about something gloriously small: principles, slippery slopes, tradition versus progress.
VIRAL: a public debate. Each advocate argues one approved position (assignment given in the case data). The judge and clerk are strictly neutral and spectator-friendly. Nobody gives betting, trading or financial advice.

TRIAL PLAN: write exactly these slots, in this order, and nothing else.
L01 (written by the court; do not write this slot): Public-case introduction with the verbatim question (written by the court, not the model).
L02 judge (opening, 25-260 characters): Neutral background: what the debate is, using only the approved summary and sources. Mark opinions as opinions. Dry, spectator-friendly.
L03 defense for Side A (opening, 70-300 characters): Side A argument: the approved Side A position at its most persuasive and entertaining.
L04 prosecutor for Side B (opening, 70-300 characters): Side B argument: the approved Side B position at its most persuasive and entertaining.
L05 prosecutor for Side B (rebuttal, 70-300 characters, answers L03): Challenge to Side A: attack the reasoning of L03 specifically.
L06 defense for Side A (rebuttal, 70-300 characters, answers L04): Challenge to Side B: attack the reasoning of L04 specifically.
L07 defense for Side A (rebuttal, 70-300 characters, answers L05): Rebuttal for Side A: answer the challenge in L05 with a new point.
L08 prosecutor for Side B (rebuttal, 70-300 characters, answers L06): Rebuttal for Side B: answer the challenge in L06 with a new point.
L09 judge (rebuttal, 25-220 characters): Comedic judge reaction to the debate itself. Even-handed.
L10 judge (closing, 25-260 characters): Balanced conclusion: one fair sentence for each side's best point. No winner, no prediction, no mention of bets, odds or money.
L11 (written by the court; do not write this slot): Resolution-pending announcement (written by the court, not the model).

Write "analysis" first, then "lines" for the model slots only (L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L07, L08, L09, L10).
LENGTH: the whole trial should take about 70-110 seconds to read: aim for 731-1331 characters across your lines, and stay inside each slot's character range. Shorter and sharper beats longer.
```
